BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANJAN MONI KALITA  ORDER Date : 04.12.2025 Heard Mr. D. Sarmah, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners.
Also heard Mr. P. Borthakur, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor, representing the State respondent.

2. This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., 1973, assailing the legality and validity of the order dated 10.08.2023, passed by the Hon'ble Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Lakhimpur, North Lakhimpur in petition no. 1441/2023, filed under Section 239 of the Cr.P.C., in P.R. Case No. 1215/2019 of Bihpuria P.S. Case NO. 261/2012 (G.R. Case No. 1502/2012),
registered under Sections 420/468/34 of the IPC.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Lakhimpur, North Lakhimpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The petitioners' case is that though the petitioners had filed a discharge petition being petition no.
1441/2023, under Section 239 of the Cr.P.C., praying for discharging them from the offences under Sections 420/468/34 of the IPC, the same was rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, North-Lakhimpur, without any valid reasons.

4. It is the case of the petitioners that though the petitioners were actually not involved in the aforesaid offences as alleged in the FIR and though there were no Page No.# 3/4 specific allegations against the petitioners, the petitioners were charge-sheeted.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the accused petitioners submits that from the statements recorded before the police, it is found that none of the victims had actually alleged any kind of cheating against the accused petitioners rather, there are certain allegations against one Rubul Gogoi, who is the husband of the accused petitioner no. 1, Bandana Gogoi.

The learned counsel further submits that though there are certain allegations against the aforesaid accused person Rubul Gogoi, he has already been discharged by the police as no charge-sheet was filed against him.

In view of the aforesaid, the learned counsel submits that since the main accused has not been charge- sheeted by the police, the order passed by the learned JMFC, North-Lakhimpur is apparently and palpably wrong whereby the petitioners were not discharged.

Therefore, he submits that the Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192226420/
2 proceedings before the learned JMFC, Lakhimpur may be stayed till the disposal of the petition.
6. Mr. P. Borthakur, learned Addl. P.P. appearing for the State submits that there is no illegality in the order passed by the learned JMFC, North-Lakhimpur.
Therefore, no interim order, as prayed for, should be granted.
7. This Court has gone through the materials brought before this Court as well as perused the Trial Court records that has been placed before this Court.

8. On perusal of the TCR as well as on considering the submissions of the counsel appearing for their respective parties, this Court is of the considered view that, at this stage, further proceedings of the P.R. Case No. 1215/2019, pending before the Court of JMFC, North-Lakhimpur, should be stayed till the disposal of the instant criminal petition.
9. In view of the aforesaid findings, the proceedings of P.R. Case No. 1215/2019, pending before the Court of JMFC, North-Lakhimpur is stayed.

10. Let the matter be listed again in the 2nd week of January, 2026.
